evidence: Much of the rubric is carefully deduplicated: hro_refusal_status counts only refused replays and sends accepted replays to their own rows (functional/judge.toml:197-203); hro_anonymous alone owns 401; the 409 status belongs only to refusal_status while hro_stale_refused grades refusal plus the actor's name; job_open/interview_full/bulk_places/undo_full each say who owns which overfill; activity vs activity_refusals, drafts vs msg_compose, pol_live_thread vs unread_scrolled_up, and pol_failed_send vs pol_session_resume all carry explicit 'graded only in' lines; hro_restart compares against a before-restart baseline recorded in D (lesson 16 applied there). I found no pair that demands incompatible products. DEFECT, same observable graded twice across dimensions: Functional hro_live_board (functional/judge.toml:296-302, weight 2) grades 'within 15 seconds this page shows the other recruiter's move in the new stage and place'. Polish hro_pol_live_board (polish/judge.toml:19-26, weight 2) has the trigger 'another recruiter moves a different card of the same job. Once the move is visible on this page (within 15 seconds, no reload)...' and says 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds, preservation cannot be shown and this row is 0'. Likewise Functional hro_msg_exchange (functional/judge.toml:305-311) grades a message appearing on Rafael's open conversation 'within 15 seconds without reload', while Polish hro_pol_live_thread (polish/judge.toml:28-35, weight 2) says 'If Noor's message does not appear within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'. The 15-second arrival bound is therefore a zeroing condition in two polish rows as well as in its functional owners. This contradicts the polish prompt's own rule 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row' (polish/prompt.md:24) and the functional 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' (functional/prompt.md:31), and it is the pattern of Colderwater lesson 16. The 'dead feature earns no credit' rule (REVIEW_POLICY) explains why the polish rows fail when no update ever arrives. It does not explain why they repeat the functional timeliness threshold: preservation can be observed on a late update. SECONDARY RISKS (wording/cascade, not independently decisive): (a) hro_candidate_view (functional/judge.toml:386-392) lists 'Tomas's ... new J2 card' among the applications whose absence fails the row, while hro_candidate_linked (409) says 'This row alone owns that link'. The T fallback in functional/prompt.md:47 reduces the clash, but the criterion text still names the J2 card. (b) hro_refused_put_back (134-140, weight 2) can only be observed on the full-Interview refusal. An app with no server capacity check and no UI precheck fails hro_interview_full and loses refused_put_back too, with no fallback to another refused move. (c) Re-order failure cascades into the literal expected orders 'Y, W, X' and '(Y, W, X, Z, A2)' in hro_bulk_move and hro_undo_restores, and into the re-order leg of hro_undo_conflict. Undo failure cascades into the undo legs of hro_reject_reason and hro_reopen. The prompt's 'a step you skipped ... fails' (prompt.md:25) conflicts with 'never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' when a setup is impossible, and no criterion says what to do then.
counterexample: A conforming-in-spirit app that polls every 20 s, with perfect draft, focus, scroll and open-card preservation and correct moves and messages. It fails hro_live_board and hro_msg_exchange in Functional, which is fair. It then also scores 0 on hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread (4.0 of 9.5 polish weight, about 0.084 reward) solely because the update arrived after 15 s, which the Functional rows already deducted. A judge following 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row' could instead pass them, so the outcome is also inconsistent between runs.
suggested_fix: In hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread, wait up to e.g. 60 s for the update, state that timeliness is graded only in hro_live_board/hro_msg_exchange, and keep 0 only when no update arrives at all. Also remove 'new J2 card' from hro_candidate_view or mark it 'scored only in hro_candidate_linked', and make the cascading legs (refused_put_back on unenforced capacity, re-order-dependent orders, undo legs in reject/reopen) say they are judged relative to the actual board order or left out when a feature graded elsewhere prevents their setup.
